label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
**Subject:** Tuesday reading club: new numbers before the 18th, and an apology

Dear Niamh,

Thank you for your email of the 30th about pausing the Tuesday club after Christmas. I understand why it came up. The numbers in September were thin, and I know the insurance on the room has gone up and that has to be weighed. But things have changed a great deal in the last few weeks, and I wanted you to have the full picture before the review meeting on Wednesday the 18th.

In September we had five children most weeks. By the middle of October we were up to nine. On Tuesday the 3rd we had fourteen in the meeting room upstairs, and I had to go down to borrow two more chairs. Word has clearly got round among the parents, and the children who come are bringing their friends.

We've also had a lovely bit of luck with books. Declan Moran of the Salthill Book Nook donated 120 books, mostly for the six to nine age group, and a good few of them as Gaeilge. The children went straight for them, and it means we're no longer passing the same dozen tired paperbacks around the circle.

The numbers only tell part of it, though. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family started with us in October. At the end of every session now, the older girl sits with her little sister and reads to her in English. The rest of the group has started to wait for it. And there's a boy who wouldn't open a book at all in September. Last week he asked me could he take two home. Forty years in the classroom and that sort of thing still stops me in my tracks.

So I'd ask you, please, to look at the pause again in light of all this. It would be a terrible pity to stop now, just as it has taken off. If the insurance cost is the sticking point, I'd be very glad to sit down with you and think about ways round it.

Now for the part I'd rather have told you in person. A couple of weeks ago I got talking to Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers' market. I was full of the club and got carried away, and I told her to come along any Tuesday. She's since been in touch and would like to come on Tuesday the 24th with a photographer.

I know perfectly well that has to go through you first, and that no child can be photographed without your sign-off and the parental consent forms. I should have checked with you before saying a word to her. I didn't, and I was wrong, plain and simple. I'd much rather you heard it from me than from anyone else.

Nothing has been agreed beyond that loose invitation, and nobody has taken any photographs. If you're happy for me to, I'll ring Orla this week and tell her the visit is on hold until you've had a chance to decide. I'll make it clear that any decision is yours.

If you do think it's worth doing, I'd be happy to look after the consent forms myself. I'd hand them out to the parents, explain what's involved, collect them back and get them to you well ahead of time, so it's no extra work at your end. I do think a piece in the Courier could be wonderful for the club, and maybe for Corrib Reading Partners more widely. But only if it's done properly, and done your way. If you'd rather leave it altogether, that's grand too, and I'll let Orla know.

I'm very glad to talk any of this over before the 18th, by phone or over a cup of tea, whichever suits you. Thank you for all you do keeping the volunteers organised. I know the decisions don't always come easy.

Warm regards,

[Your name]

---

One thing to check: you mentioned "last Tuesday (3 Nov)". By today's date the most recent Tuesday was the 10th, so I wrote "Tuesday the 3rd" to keep it accurate. If you had fourteen again on the 10th, or more, it's worth adding that in.
